rules: The government Planning Data design record for Land Registry polygons identifies the current public source as HM Land Registry's INSPIRE download service.
The Planning Data design record names gml_id as a field in the available HM Land Registry INSPIRE polygon data.
The Planning Data design record names INSPIREID as a field in the available HM Land Registry INSPIRE polygon data.
The Planning Data design record names LABEL as a field in the available HM Land Registry INSPIRE polygon data.
The Planning Data design record names NATIONALCADASTRALREFERENCE as a field in the available HM Land Registry INSPIRE polygon data.
The Planning Data design record names VALIDFROM as a field in the available HM Land Registry INSPIRE polygon data.
The Planning Data design record names BEGINLIFESPANVERSION as a field in the available HM Land Registry INSPIRE polygon data.
The Planning Data design record describes INSPIRE polygon coverage as national but packaged individually by local authority.
The Planning Data design record identifies HM Land Registry as the publisher of the available Land Registry polygon data.
The Planning Data design record says the available Land Registry polygon data is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The Planning Data design record states that one national provider, HM Land Registry, supplies the polygon data through individual local-authority packages.
The Planning Data design record requires HM Land Registry attribution for reused polygon information.
The Planning Data design record separately requires Ordnance Survey attribution for the polygon geometry using current attribution identifier AC0000851063.
The Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset contains HM Land Registry title numbers associated with Ordnance Survey AddressBase UPRNs.
The Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset covers registered properties in England and Wales only where an address association containing a UPRN can be made.
In the Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset, Title_No is a mandatory character field.
In the Title Number/UPRN Look Up dataset, UPRN is a mandatory integer field.
HM Land Registry records addresses when property is registered and attempts to link those addresses to Ordnance Survey AddressBase.
When an HM Land Registry address cannot initially be linked to AddressBase, HM Land Registry may create a new address record.
HM Land Registry can later match its created address and title number to a new AddressBase address when one becomes available.
A title number and UPRN can be linked only when HM Land Registry can establish a relationship between the AddressBase address and the title.
The Title Number/UPRN dataset is separated from National Polygon and Title Descriptor data so the products are smaller and easier to manage and maintain.
The title number is the shared unique identifier used to link the Title Number/UPRN dataset to other HM Land Registry data.
The Title Descriptor dataset contains all registered titles relating to land or property and records estate interest plus class of title.
Every registered title represented by Title Descriptor always has a title number.
Every completed registered title represented by Title Descriptor has an estate interest and class of title.
An application awaiting registration can have a title number while estate interest and class of title remain absent.
Title Descriptor includes applications for registration that HM Land Registry has started but not yet completed.
The Title Descriptor class diagram contains Title Number, Estate Interest, Class of Title, Registered Status and Change Indicator.
In Title Descriptor, Registered Status is mandatory and the value Pending indicates an application is being processed.
In Title Descriptor, a blank Registered Status indicates the title is registered.
In Title Descriptor, Change Indicator is mandatory and can represent New, Changed or Deleted rows.
Estate Interest code EL means Estate in land.
Estate Interest code FA means Affecting franchise.
Estate Interest code FC means Relating franchise.
Absolute freehold class code AF is documented as the best class of freehold title.
Qualified freehold class code QF can be used where a specific defect prevents grant of absolute title.
Possessory freehold class code PF can be used for adverse-possession claims or where title deeds have been lost or destroyed.
HM Land Registry states that tenure of a title does not change within the Title Descriptor maintenance model.
A non-absolute class of title can be upgraded when an application is made with the required evidence.
Title Descriptor publishes a full extract every month.
Title Descriptor publishes a change-only update every month.
Title Descriptor publishes a validation file every month to check that data downloaded correctly.
Title Descriptor files are updated and available from the second working day of each month.
Title Descriptor full-file naming follows LR_TENURE_FULL_<3 character Month>, with separate change-only and validation naming conventions.
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in CSV format.
Planning Data bulk downloads are available in JSON format.
Planning Data bulk downloads can be available in GeoJSON where applicable.
Planning Data bulk downloads can be available in Parquet.
Planning Data explicitly describes Parquet as well suited to large datasets.
Planning Data recommends coordinate queries for checking planning constraints at a specific location.
A Planning Data coordinate query can request more than one dataset in the same call.
When multiple dataset parameters are supplied, Planning Data returns matching entities from any selected dataset.
Planning Data documents conservation-area as a dataset that can be screened by coordinate.
Planning Data documents listed-building as a dataset that can be screened by coordinate.
Planning Data documents green-belt as a dataset that can be screened by coordinate.
Planning Data documents flood-risk-zone as a dataset that can be screened by coordinate.
Planning Data documents article-4-direction-area as a dataset that can be screened by coordinate.
Planning Data documents tree-preservation-zone as a dataset that can be screened by coordinate.
Planning Data recommends grouping returned constraints by dataset when presenting coordinate-screening results.
Raw WKT polygon queries to Planning Data use WGS84 EPSG:4326 coordinates.
Planning Data requires spaces in a WKT query string to be percent-encoded, while noting that most HTTP client libraries handle this automatically.
Planning Data uses the offset parameter to paginate large entity result sets.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the limit value for successive pages.
Planning Data responses provide a pre-built next pagination link.
Planning Data responses provide a pre-built previous pagination link.
Planning Data responses provide a pre-built first-page link.
Planning Data responses provide a pre-built last-page link.
Planning Data's portfolio-screening guidance states that the API has no batch endpoint.
For API-based portfolio screening, Planning Data recommends issuing one request per property.
Planning Data recommends using field filters to reduce portfolio-screening responses to needed attributes.
The documented portfolio example requests the name, dataset and reference fields.
The documented portfolio example uses a result limit of 50.
Planning Data explicitly recommends polite rate-limiting between per-property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk dataset downloads rather than repeated per-property API calls.
For large portfolios, Planning Data recommends performing spatial intersections locally against downloaded datasets.
Planning Data describes bulk downloads as providing a stable snapshot for large-portfolio processing.
Planning Data warns that bulk download URL formats vary by dataset.
The Planning Data single-entity API supports JSON output.
The Planning Data single-entity API supports GeoJSON output.
The Planning Data single-entity API supports HTML output.
The Planning Data dataset-list API supports JSON output.
The Planning Data dataset-list API supports HTML output.
The Planning Data dataset-list include_typologies parameter can be set false to omit typologies from JSON output.
Planning Data publishes an OpenAPI JSON description that can be used to generate a client library with tools such as Swagger Editor.
The current Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 1 metre spatial resolution.
The current LIDAR Composite DTM 1m was produced by the Environment Agency in 2022.
The DTM 1m combines Environment Agency Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
For repeat survey coverage in the DTM 1m composite, the newest and best-resolution data is selected.
Where source data required resampling for the DTM 1m composite, bilinear interpolation was used before merging.
The 2022 DTM 1m composite contains source surveys undertaken between 6 June 2000 and 2 April 2022.
The DTM 1m metadata directs users to survey-index catalogues to determine which source survey was used at a location.
The DTM 1m is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters.
The DTM 1m is distributed in 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM 1m elevations are expressed in metres.
DTM 1m elevations are referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The DTM 1m composite uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
The individual LIDAR surveys contributing to the DTM 1m composite are documented with vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The DTM 1m record declares no public access constraints beyond its identified licence.
The DTM 1m is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The DTM 1m metadata declares annual update frequency.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m geographic metadata extent is latitude 49.943 to 55.816.
The DTM 1m geographic metadata extent is longitude -6.236 to 2.072.
The DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The Environment Agency DTM 1m record exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services plus an OGC API Features service.
The LIDAR Composite DSM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DSM 1m is generated from the last or only laser return and retains surface objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
The DSM 1m combines Time Stamped archive data with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
The DSM 1m uses newest, best-resolution data where surveys repeat and bilinear interpolation where resampling is required.
The DSM 1m composite source period is 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
The DSM 1m record exposes WCS and WMTS access in addition to downloadable survey data.
The LIDAR Composite DSM 2m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 2 metre spatial resolution.
The DSM 2m metadata identifier is f083c5dc-504f-4428-9811-a1b2519fa279.
The DSM 2m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DSM 2m geographic metadata extent is latitude 49.943 to 55.816.
The DSM 2m geographic metadata extent is longitude -6.236 to 2.072.
The First Return DSM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England at 1 metre spatial resolution.
The First Return DSM 1m is produced from the first or only laser return.
The First Return DSM 1m can include vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
The First Return DSM 1m is based on National LIDAR Programme capture from 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022.
The National LIDAR Programme divided England into roughly 300 survey blocks over continuous winters from 2016 onward for the first-return composite.
First-return composite surveys are merged using feathering at overlaps to reduce small elevation differences.
The First Return DSM coverage can differ from the last-return DSM because the last-return composite also incorporates Time Stamped surveys.
The First Return DSM 1m is supplied as 5 kilometre GeoTIFF tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
The First Return DSM 1m record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features access.
The First Return DSM 2m uses the same National LIDAR Programme 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022 source period.
The DTM 10m is resampled from the LIDAR Composite DTM 2m dataset.
The DTM 10m resampling method is bilinear interpolation.
The DTM 10m is a terrain rather than surface-object model, with surface objects removed through the DTM production process.
The National LIDAR Programme survey-data record states that all available derived products use 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the Ordnance Survey grid.
National LIDAR Programme tile names can encode the unique survey identifier, OS grid reference, first survey date and last survey date.
National LIDAR Programme surface models are supplied as GeoTIFF rasters.
National LIDAR Programme point-cloud data is supplied in compressed LAZ format.
The National LIDAR Programme First Return DSM is more likely than a last-return product to capture the top or near-top of trees and building edges.
The Environment Agency notes that First Return DSM data can support canopy-height modelling.
The Environment Agency notes that First Return DSM data can support production of building outlines.
The National LIDAR Programme Intensity Surface Model measures reflected laser-light intensity from each pulse.
Intensity values depend in part on the near-infrared wavelength used.
Intensity values also vary with the composition of the reflecting surface.
Intensity values also vary with angle of incidence.
The Intensity Surface Model is rendered as a grayscale representation.
In the intensity model, darker surfaces such as roads can reflect less laser light than surfaces such as vegetation.
The National LIDAR Programme coverage metadata is available as full downloads in file geodatabase format.
The National LIDAR Programme coverage metadata is available as full downloads in GeoJSON format.
The National LIDAR Programme coverage metadata is available as full downloads in GeoPackage format.
The National LIDAR Programme coverage metadata is available as full downloads in Shapefile format.
The National LIDAR Programme metadata record has a revision date of 15 December 2023.
The National LIDAR Programme metadata period extends through 5 May 2023.
The retired 25 centimetre LIDAR Composite DTM has been replaced by the 1 metre composite while 25 centimetre time-stamped archive data remains available through the survey archive.
The OS Downloads API can be used to discover available OS OpenData products.
The OS Downloads API can provide metadata for available OS OpenData products.
The OS Downloads API can provide download links for OS OpenData products.
The OS Downloads API can automate retrieval and integration of Ordnance Survey data into other systems.
The OS Downloads API supports automated access to both OpenData and Premium datasets.
The OS Downloads API supports multiple download formats including GeoTIFF, CSV and GeoPackage where offered by a product.
The OS Downloads API can request different coverage areas depending on the OpenData dataset.
The OS Downloads API can request different formats depending on the OpenData dataset.
The OS Downloads API can return thumbnail-image metadata for OpenData products.
The OS Downloads API does not provide previous releases of OpenData datasets.
The OS Downloads API cannot create new Premium data packages.
The OS Downloads API cannot alter existing data packages.
For Premium-data downloads, the OS Downloads API getting-started guidance requires an API project with an API key.
The OpenData product-list endpoint is GET /products.
The OpenData product-list endpoint can use expanded=true to return full product details in the list response.
The OpenData product-list endpoint returns successful results as application/json.
OpenData product details are retrieved with GET /products/{productId}.
The productId path value is required for the OpenData product-details endpoint.
An OpenData product-details request returns 404 when it does not match known content.
OpenData downloads are enumerated with GET /products/{productId}/downloads.
The OpenData downloads endpoint requires productId.
The OpenData downloads endpoint can filter by fileName.
The OpenData downloads endpoint can filter by format.
The OpenData downloads endpoint can filter by subformat.
The OpenData downloads endpoint can filter by geographic area.
The OpenData downloads area enumeration includes GB for all of Great Britain.
The OpenData downloads area enumeration includes TQ as a National Grid reference square.
If redirect is requested and exactly one OpenData download matches, the endpoint returns a 307 redirect to the actual download.
Without a single redirected match, a successful OpenData download-list request returns JSON with HTTP 200.
An OpenData downloads request that matches no known content returns HTTP 404 with a human-readable message and may include navigation links.
OpenData product images are retrieved with GET /products/{productId}/images/{index}.
The OpenData product-image endpoint requires both productId and image index.
Valid product-image indices run from zero through Product.imageCount minus one.
The product-image endpoint supports a large boolean to request a larger image.
A product-image request can return JPEG image data.
A product-image request can return HTTP 307 redirecting to the actual image location.
OS Terrain 50 documentation describes the product as an open height dataset for Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 documentation lists spot heights as part of the open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 documentation lists breaklines as part of the open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 documentation lists coastline as part of the open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 documentation lists lakes as part of the open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 documentation lists ridges as part of the open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 documentation lists formlines as part of the open height dataset.
OS Terrain 50 has a nominal 1:50,000 scale in the product documentation.
OS Terrain 50's data theme is height.
OS Terrain 50's 50 metre post spacing is intended to model the entire landscape at lower resolution.
The Terrain 50 surface model includes significant landscape features such as major roads.
The Terrain 50 surface model includes large lakes.
The Terrain 50 surface model includes estuaries.
OS Terrain 50 provides free sample viewing for Exeter, Newport and Inverness through the OS MasterMap Product Viewer.

The three candidates still lack candidate-specific valid HM Land Registry INSPIRE IDs proven by exact native-British-National-Grid polygon containment; schema knowledge alone is not sufficient for identity promotion.
Exact coordinate responses for the three candidates remain unread because parameterized Planning Data candidate URLs are blocked by execution URL safety.
Exact reference-filter responses for parcel refs 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remain uncaptured; search-index absence is not promoted to NO_DATA.
The exact TQ2892 filtered survey-feature response remains unread, so survey-date/resolution provenance cannot yet be bound to each candidate.
The exact candidate WCS GetCoverage GeoTIFF bytes, SHA-256, NoData filtering and numeric elevations remain unread; product-level accuracy and metadata are not candidate heights.

Current Terrain50 TQ29 download bytes, SHA-256 and row149 col173/174 numeric values remain absent, so no Terrain50 numeric cross-check is promoted.
